audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic and their interfaces. EL topics include EVM operations (bitwise, trie, initcode limits, secp256r1 precompile, fork activations, blob transaction distribution). CL topics include merge transition, payload validation, P2P fork versioning, proposer-builder separation, and slashing mechanics.

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, oversized initcode, resource exhaustion attacks via gas underpricing
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, blob data withholding, propagation attacks

el_attack_vectors.entry_point: EVM Execution (CALL, CREATE, CREATE2, precompile calls)
el_attack_vectors.threat: Exploit precompile edge cases, initcode abuse, state trie manipulation via key grinding

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks with bad execution payloads, submit conflicting attestations, equivocation
Provide invalid bids, withhold payloads after proposer commitment, collude to censor transactions
Return incorrect validation results, causing CL to accept invalid execution payloads

misclassified_entities.reason: Development process entity (specification author), not a runtime external entity interacting with the system at execution time
Abstract internal concept representing trie key sources; not a distinct external entity — keys originate from transactions which are already modeled
Internal EVM execution context, not an external entity. The external source is the transaction submitter, not the transaction itself
The mempool is internal node state. User transactions entering the mempool are already covered by the User via JSON-RPC entity

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary messages including malformed transactions, invalid blobs, or fabricated blob data. Covers EIP-8094 blob separation and general tx propagation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via CL Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: libp2p gossipsub (beacon blocks, attestations, P2P fork-versioned messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL peers are unauthenticated at the network level. Covers EIP-7928 fork version selection and general CL P2P messaging. Malicious peers can send messages with wrong fork versions.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via public RPC endpoints with no authentication. Covers contract deployment (EIP-3860 initcode limits), transaction replay attempts (EIP-607/EIP-155), and general transaction submission. All input must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The CL trusts the EL to correctly validate execution payloads (Bellatrix merge transition). However, a buggy or compromised EL could return incorrect validation results. Content must still be logically validated by CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The EL receives execution payloads and fork choice updates from the CL. While authenticated, the EL must validate payload content (parent hash, timestamp, RANDAO, transactions).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block proposals via P2P gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks containing execution payloads. A malicious proposer may include invalid payloads, attempt equivocation, or exploit merge transition edge cases. Covers Bellatrix payload validation and slashing mechanics.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV Relay via Builder API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The relay mediates between builders and proposers. It is trusted to validate payloads, select highest bids, and reveal payloads after signing. However, a compromised relay can withhold payloads, return invalid bids, or collude with builders. Authentication exists but trust in behavior is assumed.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Builder via MEV Relay
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builders submit execution payload bids competing in block auctions. Builders are untrusted — they may submit invalid payloads, undervalued bids, or attempt censorship. The relay is expected to validate builder submissions.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV Searcher via Builder
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Searchers identify MEV opportunities and submit bundles. They are untrusted external actors who may attempt sandwich attacks, front-running, or other extractive strategies.

trusted_external_entities.name: Slashing Evidence Reporter via Beacon Block
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: ProposerSlashing / AttesterSlashing operations in beacon blocks
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any validator can include slashing evidence in blocks. The evidence itself must be cryptographically verified — the reporter is untrusted but evidence validity is independently checkable.

trusted_external_entities.name: WebAuthn/FIDO2 Device via Smart Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External hardware devices generate secp256r1 signatures that are passed through smart contracts to the precompile. The signature data is untrusted — all cryptographic validation (input length, curve membership, bounds checks) must be performed. Covers EIP-7951.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Pre-Merge Miner)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Pre-merge miners produce blocks that trigger fork activations (EIP-607 Spurious Dragon). Miners are untrusted — blocks must pass all consensus rules for the applicable fork.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received transactions must be fully validated (signature, nonce, gas, initcode size per EIP-3860). Blob transactions received without sidecars must not be forwarded until all blobs are fetched and validated (EIP-8094).

Blob data received via PooledBlobs must have hash correspondence validated against requested vhashes. Missing or mismatched blobs must be handled gracefully. Nodes MUST NOT forward transactions with unvalidated blobs.

All P2P messages must use correct fork version encoding (EIP-7928). Messages with incorrect fork versions must be rejected. Fork version is determined by epoch threshold checks in strict descending order.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, chain ID check (EIP-155 replay protection), initcode size <= 49152 bytes for creation transactions (EIP-3860), gas limit >= intrinsic gas including initcode cost, contract code size <= 24KB (EIP-170).

CL relies on EL to correctly execute and validate payloads. The Engine API channel is JWT-authenticated. CL still validates parent_hash consistency, RANDAO, timestamp, and no-empty-transactions constraint independently before delegating full execution validation to EL (Bellatrix).

EL must validate execution payload content (transaction validity, state transitions, gas accounting) regardless of CL authentication. JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but not content correctness.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon block proposal via P2P gossip
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Proposed blocks must pass full validation: execution payload checks (parent hash, RANDAO, timestamp), signature verification, slot/epoch consistency. Equivocating proposers must be slashed.

Relay is expected to return valid, highest-value bids and reveal full payloads after proposer commitment. Proposer should implement fallback to local block building if relay is unresponsive. Relay failure after signing results in missed slot (liveness risk).
Builder payloads must be validated by the relay before being presented to proposers. Invalid payloads, censored blocks, or undervalued bids should be filtered by relay validation.
Searcher bundles are untrusted transaction orderings. Standard transaction validation applies to all individual transactions within bundles.

Slashing evidence must be cryptographically verified (conflicting signatures from same validator). Reporter identity is irrelevant — evidence validity is independently verifiable. Bellatrix parameters: MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT=32, PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER=3.

Input must be exactly 160 bytes. Signature bounds (0 < r,s < n), public key field bounds (0 <= qx,qy < p), curve equation membership, and non-identity point checks are all required. Gas (6900) is consumed regardless of validation outcome. Signatures are malleable (both (r,s) and (r,n-s) valid) per EIP-7951.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific rules. At block 2,675,000 (Spurious Dragon), EIP-155 replay protection, EIP-160 EXP cost, EIP-161 state clearing, and EIP-170 code size limits activate. All blocks must meet applicable rule set.
